source.title: Code Isn't Memory: A Structural Codebase Index Inside a Coding Agent
source.summary: Coding agents now interleave LLMs with retrieval over the working repository, and retrieval implementations vary widely across deployed harnesses. Inside a fixed coding-agent harness on a fixed model, does adding a structural codebase index actually change cost or resolve? We ran three arms (the harness with the index, the same harness without it, and an agentic-grep comparator) on SWE-PolyBench Verified and SWE-bench Pro with Claude Opus 4.7 held fixed throughout, across three seeds, inside a leak-audited per-task sandbox. The within-harness ablation produces a large localization gain and a statistically separated resolve gain, with no cost penalty per cell and lower cost per solve. The cross-harness check shows that the index does not regress against an agentic-grep baseline on resolve or localization, again at no cost penalty. We release the per-cell exclusion ledger, the leak-audit script, the localization extractor, and the results database. The deployment question for a structural codebase index is thus not whether it is too expensive to run (across seeds, the index lands at a lower $/solved than agentic grep) but whether the workload includes multi-file changes where structural ranking pays off.

previous_facts.title: Code Isn't Memory: A Structural Codebase Index Inside a Coding Agent
previous_facts.event_hint: arXiv paper (SuperAGI Research) giving the first leak-audited, model-controlled causal ablation of a structural codebase index (semantic+lexical+call-graph) inside the open-source SuperCoder coding-agent harness, versus the same harness without it and an agentic-grep (OpenCode) comparator.
previous_facts.problem: Coding agents interleave LLMs with repository retrieval, but retrieval implementations vary widely across harnesses and there is no clean causal answer to whether adding a structural codebase index changes cost or resolve. Prior work either compares whole harnesses (confounding retrieval with prompt, tool surface, and control loop) or evaluates retrieval components in isolation on acc@k without the downstream agentic loop that turns ranking into a fix.
previous_facts.mechanism: Three arms run on the same instance set with the model held fixed (Claude Opus 4.7): SC-ON (SuperCoder harness with context-engine tools codebase_search and codebase_graph available), SC-OFF (same harness, same prompts, with exactly those two engine tools removed), and OpenCode (an independent harness whose retrieval is ripgrep + file reads, no structural index). The within-harness SC-ON vs SC-OFF toggle isolates the index causally. Localization is scored under 'View B' (agent-targeted), which strips paths whose only provenance is an engine result list so that SC-ON acc@k counts the same agent-targeted surface as a grep arm; the rule is a strict no-op for SC-OFF/OpenCode (Algorithm 1, §4.7).

evidence.claim: Within-harness ablation: View B acc@5 localization moves from 44.3% (SC-OFF) to 84.5% (SC-ON), paired Wilcoxon p < 0.0001.
evidence.condition: SuperCoder harness, Claude Opus 4.7, 3 seeds, View B localization, SWE-PolyBench Verified + SWE-bench Pro; pairwise n=80 (SC-ON vs SC-OFF)

evidence.claim: Within-harness ablation: resolve moves from 41.9% (SC-OFF) to 50.4% (SC-ON), paired p = 0.003; per-cell mean cost is statistically null (p = 0.73) while turns and tokens both fall significantly.
evidence.condition: same harness/model/seeds; resolve = F2P pass and P2P pass per upstream benchmark scorers

evidence.claim: Cross-harness check vs agentic-grep: SC-ON vs OpenCode on resolve (p = 0.087) and View B acc@5 (p = 0.080) is directional in SC-ON's favor but NOT conventionally significant (marginal). The within-harness ablation is the cleaner read.
evidence.condition: 3 seeds, pairwise n=78 (SC-ON vs OpenCode); across-seed SD 0.7-3.3 pp on resolve and acc@5, ablation effects exceed noise by 3-10x
evidence.source_locator: §7 Discussion / 'What we do not claim', PDF Page 9

evidence.claim: Cost/effort: per-cell mean cost is statistically null while turns and tokens both fall significantly; across seeds the index lands at a lower $/solved than agentic grep (no cost penalty per cell, lower cost per solve).
evidence.condition: unified provider gateway captured token-level cost on every LLM call, same accounting across arms

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Model fixed throughout: Claude Opus 4.7 (claude-opus-4-7), 3 seeds, pass@1 per seed; stats reported as mean of seed means with across-seed SD. Benchmarks: SWE-PolyBench Verified (Go, Java, Python) + SWE-bench Pro (long-context Python). Run scope: 91 instances (34 Go, 20 Java, 37 Python); JS/TS not covered. Paired-n: triple-intersection n=75; pairwise n=80 (SC-ON vs SC-OFF), n=78 (SC-ON vs OpenCode). 30-minute wall-clock cap, no turn/dollar cap; cap fired on two cells (one SC-OFF, one OpenCode); SC-ON's longest legit cell ran 19 min. Per-task isolated container, uniform image across arms, leak-audited sandbox; released artifacts include per-cell exclusion ledger, leak-audit script, dual-view localization extractor, and full results DB (per-cell patches/traces/prompts held back due to licensed source + internal config).
previous_facts.limitations: Single-model study (only Claude Opus 4.7) — intentional control trade, acknowledged as a limitation. Closed-source harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) out of scope by design. JavaScript/TypeScript not covered. The cross-harness SC-ON vs OpenCode result on resolve (p=0.087) and acc@5 (p=0.080) is marginal, NOT conventionally significant — the within-harness ablation is the cleaner read. The substantive benefit is conditional: the deployment question is whether the workload includes multi-file changes where structural ranking pays off, not whether the index is too expensive to run. Does not address the phrasing-ecological-validity threat (Garg et al. >50% capability overestimation).
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly on the Agent-semantic-acceleration card: it causally tests whether a structural codebase index reduces repeated search/read effort and improves task success, and reports exactly the card's valuable evidence — tool-call count (turns), token consumption, resolve rate, and $/solved. The finding that turns and tokens both fall significantly while per-cell cost stays null and $/solved drops is concrete evidence that the index cuts repeated Read/Grep-style exploration, answering the card's core question. The marginal cross-harness result and single-model scope are the boundary the briefing must flag before generalizing.
source_notes: Source: arXiv 2606.22417v1, SuperAGI Research (Ishaan Bhola, Adithyan Krishnan, Sravanth Kurmala, Mukunda NS), fetch_status=FETCHED, raw_fulltext_cache_hit=true.

Evidence Pack spans PDF Pages 1, 2, 4, 5, 9: abstract, intro, related work, experimental design (arms/model/benchmarks/sandbox/metrics/localization views), and the §7 Discussion with the headline ablation numbers and explicit 'what we do not claim' caveats.
